title: Nrf2 expression in adenocarcinoma of the upper gastrointestinal tract – prospective analysis of the influence of perioperative and palliative systemic therapy on the Nrf2 pathway and its relevance for oncological outcome
summary:
Cancer of the oesophagus, the junction between oesophagus and stomach, and the stomach (so-called adenocarcinoma) is usually treated first with chemotherapy, sometimes combined with immunotherapy, and then with surgery. Some tumours respond very well to this pre-treatment, others hardly at all. Until now, how well the treatment has worked can only be assessed after surgery, in the removed tissue – at a point when the therapy can no longer be changed. In this study we investigate a protein in the tumour called Nrf2. We want to find out whether the amount of this protein indicates, even before treatment starts, how well chemotherapy and immunotherapy will work, and how the treatment in turn affects this protein.
For this purpose, additional tissue and blood samples are taken at two time points: during the gastroscopy performed for diagnosis and, if surgery takes place, from the already removed surgical specimen. In addition, clinical data from routine follow-up are collected for up to six years. The treatment itself is not changed by the study and no additional hospital visits are required. Participants have no direct personal benefit; the results are intended to allow future patients to receive treatment better tailored to them.
conditions: malignant diseases of the oesophagus (C15.ff), malignancies of the proximal stomach (16.0)

interventions.name:
Curative cohort (n = 30)
Patients with adenocarcinoma of the oesophagus, the gastro-oesophageal junction (AEG I–III) or the stomach scheduled for oncological resection with curative intent and receiving perioperative systemic therapy according to clinical standard of care (FLOT or D-FLOT).
Study-s

Palliative cohort (n = 10)
Patients with metastatic disease receiving palliative systemic therapy according to clinical standard of care (e.g. nivolumab, pembrolizumab, trastuzumab or zolbetuximab depending on immunohistology).
Study-specific procedures: tissue sample and blood draw at diagnosis (

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
●	Histologically confirmed or highly suspected adenocarcinoma of the oesophagus, the gastro-oesophageal junction (AEG I–III according to Siewert) or the stomach
●	Planned oncological resection with curative intent (curative cohort) or planned palliative systemic therapy (palliative cohort)
●	Age ≥ 18 years at the time of consent
●	Written informed consent
●	Sufficient tissue available for study purposes without compromising routine pathological diagnostics

Non-German-speaking patients are not excluded per se; inclusion requires complete information and consent in a language the person reliably understands, involving a qualified interpreter where necessary.
Exclusion criteria:
●	No adenocarcinoma of the oesophagus, the gastro-oesophageal junction or the stomach (e.g. squamous cell carcinoma, GIST, lymphoma, no carcinoma)
●	Lack of capacity to consent (e.g. dementia without preserved natural capacity of understanding, legal guardianship)
●	Pregnancy or breastfeeding
●	Refusal to participate in the study
●	Insufficient amount of tissue for determination of the primary endpoint, even after study-specific sampling (option A or B) or in routine material (option C)
